📰 General

iPhone Duo Arrives: CNET Tests Apple’s Foldable Device Against the Galaxy Z Fold 8 •

Apple’s iPhone Duo was released on Friday, immediately leading to sellouts and significant customer demand at Apple Stores. CNET conducted a three-hour test at the Louisville, Kentucky Apple Store to acquire a testing unit. The team evaluated the device’s performance and features, focusing on its capabilities compared to existing foldable phones. Initial observations centered on the device’s design and functionality, with a particular emphasis on its display and hinge mechanism.

🌍 World

Thousands Protest in Tel Aviv, Demanding Accountability for Israel’s Response •

Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Tel Aviv to protest against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of upcoming elections. The rally was organized by the October Council, a group comprised of families of hostages and victims of the October 7th Hamas attack. Protesters are calling for accountability regarding the events leading up to the attack and Israel’s subsequent actions in Gaza. The demonstration highlights growing public dissatisfaction with the government’s handling of the conflict and its impact on the country.

🦅 US

Veteran Filmmaker Laika Details 20-Year Journey to Create ‘Wildwood’ •

Animator Caleb Deschanel, known for his extensive work in Hollywood, spent over two decades developing the stop-motion animated film “Wildwood.” Deschanel’s career includes significant contributions to films like “The Passion of the Christ” and “The Patriot,” alongside work on iconic sequences in “The Godfather” and “Titanic.” The project’s lengthy creation process reflects a meticulous approach to storytelling and visual design. “Wildwood” marks a significant culmination of Deschanel’s artistic vision and dedication to the craft of animation.

💰 Business

Six Flags Announces Seat Belts for Goliath Roller Coaster Following Fatal Accident •

Six Flags Over Georgia has announced plans to install seat belts on the Goliath roller coaster following the death of a man who was ejected from the ride. The incident occurred earlier this month, resulting in the man falling to his death. The theme park stated that this decision was made as a safety precaution. Investigations into the specific circumstances surrounding the accident are ongoing.

💻 Technology

Ecto-1: 5 Surprising Facts Behind the Iconic Ghostbusters Vehicle •

The Ecto-1, featured in the 1984 film Ghostbusters, began its life as a 1959 Cadillac Miller-Dawson ambulance. Originally purchased by Columbia Pictures for use in filming various productions, the vehicle was later modified and became synonymous with the Ghostbusters franchise. The Cadillac’s distinctive appearance, including its siren and flashing lights, was crucial to the film’s success and has remained a beloved symbol within the pop culture landscape. Several versions of the Ecto-1 have been used throughout the franchise’s history, each with unique modifications.

🎭 Entertainment

Bill Maher’s Trump-Friendly Dinner Raises Questions on ‘Real Time’ •

Bill Maher attended a recent White House dinner alongside Kid Rock and Stephen A. Smith, an event initiated by President Trump. Following the dinner, Trump reportedly discussed the gathering with reporters, signaling a continued connection between Maher and the former president’s inner circle. The appearance marks a notable shift for Maher, who has previously been critical of Trump and his supporters. This interaction has sparked discussion regarding Maher’s evolving relationship with Trumpworld and its potential implications for his HBO show, “Real Time.”

🏅 Sports

Nick Bosa’s Extended Absence Threatens 49ers Roster Depth Ahead of Atlanta Game •

49ers defensive end Nick Bosa is sidelined with a persistent calf injury, now expected to miss his fifth game on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. Despite not being placed on injured reserve, Bosa’s absence has created roster concerns for the team. The injury has significantly reduced the 49ers’ available healthy players. This situation raises questions about the team’s depth and potential impact on their performance.

🔬 Science

Cancer Cells Triggered to Self-Destruct by Compression, Scientists Discover •

Researchers at Fudan University, Sun Yat-sen University, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a mechanism by which cancer cells initiate self-destruction. The study revealed that applying pressure or confining cancer cells within tight spaces induces a programmed cell death process. Scientists observed that this compression triggers a cascade of events leading to the cells’ demise. This discovery offers potential insights into new therapeutic strategies targeting cellular stress responses within tumors.

🩺 Health

Bird Flu Outbreak on Mink Farm Raises Concerns About Potential Human Pandemic Risk •

A highly pathogenic strain of avian influenza is devastating a mink farm in Utah, resulting in the deaths of two individuals who contracted the virus from infected animals. Scientists have confirmed that the virus remains primarily a “bird” flu, exhibiting limited ability to transmit between humans and other animals. Despite the confirmed human fatalities and the potential for the virus to mutate and become more transmissible, current U.S. officials have not implemented preventative measures or expanded surveillance. Researchers are closely monitoring the situation, recognizing the possibility of a future human pandemic if the virus continues to evolve.
